In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the problem of the prediction of gas-chromatographic retention indices of organic compounds.
the development and validation of a general approach to the prediction (and calculation) of gas chromatographic RI values for any organic compound.
the prediction of RI values from the physico-chemical properties of organic compounds, which are of interest in the analysis of complex mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RI values of organic compounds are determined by their boiling temperature and the number of carbon atoms, and the latter parameter is not an independent variable but a consequence of the boiling temperature.
the proposed approach is a reliable and convenient method of calculating RI values of organic compounds on polydimethylsilxane stationary phases, and it can be recommended for practical use.

, for the prediction of the retention indices of organic compounds on polydimethylsilicon stationary phases, the boiling temperature of the compound and the molecular weight of the stationary phase must be taken into consideration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the prediction of RI values of any organic compound is possible with a precision comparable with the standard deviation of experimental data, provided that the dependence of the logarithm of RI on the additive molecular parameter is considered.

the RI value of a substance is not a constant, but is dependent on the physico-chemical properties of the compound and the conditions of the experiment (the type of column, the carrier gas and its flow rate, the temperature of the column and of the injector, the type of the detector, etc.).

a combination of logical criteria can be used for comparing functions of physico-chemical parameters of organic compounds for the identification of compounds whose retention indices are only determined by the boiling temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dependence of the retention indices on the boiling point or molecular parameters can be used to predict the gas chromatographic behaviour of organic compounds.

the RI value of an organic compound is determined by the boiling temperature and the additive molecular parameter, which are the most important parameters for the prediction of the retention time in gas chromatography.

the RI values of organic compounds can be calculated with a precision comparable with that of the experimental determination of the retention index, provided that the dependence of the index on the additive molecular parameter is taken into consideration.
